suitability_reason: Income inclusion of conceded interest and retirement distribution, 72(t) 10% tax (under 59 1/2, no exception), and 6662 substantial-understatement threshold are mechanical; only reasonable cause is judgmental.

taxpayer.notes: Took COVID-related hardship withdrawal from Fidelity retirement account while under 59 1/2.

notice_of_deficiency.contested_by_taxpayer: Concedes receipt but argues a denied 2017 refund claim should offset 2021 liability; disputes penalty.
conceded: Petitioner conceded receipt of the $99 interest income and the $56,673 retirement distribution

findings_of_fact.fact: Hardship withdrawal of $56,673 from Fidelity retirement account in 2021; under age 59 1/2 at the time
findings_of_fact.snippet: He subsequently took a hardship withdrawal of $56,673 from his Fidelity Investments (Fidelity) retirement account.

findings_of_fact.fact: Received $99 of interest income from the IRS in 2021
findings_of_fact.snippet: He also received $99 of interest income from the IRS in 2021.

findings_of_fact.fact: Return reported $37,964 taxable income; did not report the interest, the distribution, the 10% additional tax, or $1,874 Fidelity withholding
findings_of_fact.snippet: He reported $37,964 of taxable income . He did not report the $99 of interest income or the $56,673 retirement distribution.

findings_of_fact.fact: No section 72(t) exception applies and petitioner does not argue one
findings_of_fact.snippet: None of the several exceptions to this rule apply here, nor does petitioner argue they should.

findings_of_fact.fact: Understatement of $18,064 exceeds 10% of tax required to be shown and $5,000
findings_of_fact.snippet: Respondent determined an understatement of tax of $18,064, exceeding 10% of the tax required to be shown on the return and $5,000.

findings_of_fact.fact: Penalty was automatically calculated through electronic means (6751(b)(2)(B) exception)
findings_of_fact.snippet: penalties “automatically calculated through electronic means,” such as the penalty at issue here, are excepted from the procedural requirements.

findings_of_fact.fact: Petitioner believed Fidelity would withhold the 10% tax; did not rely on a professional or consult Form 1099-R
findings_of_fact.snippet: he incorrectly believed that Fidelity would withhold and remit the requisite amount .

issues.question: Did petitioner receive and fail to report $99 of interest income for 2021?
issues.holding: Yes; receipt conceded; includible. Court lacks jurisdiction to offset a 2017 refund claim.
issues.computable_reason: Conceded receipt; interest is gross income per §61(a).

issues.question: Did petitioner receive and fail to report a $56,673 retirement distribution for 2021?
issues.holding: Yes; receipt conceded; includible in 2021 gross income.

issues.question: Is petitioner liable for the 10% additional tax of $5,667 under section 72(t)?
issues.holding: Yes; under 59 1/2 and no exception applies.
issues.computable_reason: 10% x $56,673 with age < 59 1/2 and no exception.

issues.question: Is petitioner liable for the $3,238 section 6662(a) accuracy-related penalty?
issues.holding: Yes; substantial understatement ($18,064 exceeds 10% and $5,000); 6751(b) exception for automatically calculated penalties; no reasonable cause.
issues.computable_reason: Threshold is arithmetic, but outcome also turned on 6751(b) and a reasonable-cause judgment.

decision.text: Decision will be entered for respondent.

notes: Facts stipulated at trial. Tax required to be shown on return not stated; opinion only states understatement exceeds 10% of it. Derived: 10% x $56,673 = $5,667.30; 20% x $18,064 = $3,612.80 vs $3,238 penalty determined (penalty base presumably reduced, e.g. by $1,874 withholding; derived: 20% x ($18,064 - $1,874) = $3,238). Prior ruling: no jurisdiction over 2017.
